source: Actual Windows Electron controlled by @oai/sky SendInput/UIA. Actual daemon/SQLite/SDK with fixed local SSE; tools/extensions disabled.

exclusions.label: initial-ready
exclusions.reason: Covered by another application; screenshot/UIA excluded from evidence.

exclusions.label: long-session-open
exclusions.reason: Immediate transitional state still showing new draft; settled state used.

limitations: Some immediate UIA snapshots lag the screenshot; settled captures determine outcomes.
First right-edge drag selected text and did not resize. Later Alt+Space > Size > Right > click produced an 802x961 captured native window, not the earlier attempt.
Full-screen resolution is not claimed: native maximized screenshot is 1920x1032 on the 1920x1080 display. Automated scroll light/dark are 1440x960 and 800x760.

Pagination rows are explicitly synthetic file messages appended only after SDK shutdown, not SDK-produced conversation content. The initial managed observation for that modified file can diagnose an inconsistent prior binding; dedicated read-only history is used for pagination.
Production approvals are not implemented here; synthetic approval over real TCP observation is covered by Electron E2E only.
Text input used literal SendInput, not an independent IME vendor acceptance. Existing IME regression remains in full CI.
Window bookmarks restore within the same window/sessionStorage through eviction and renderer reload; full application restart does not promise drafts or reading bookmarks.

checks.messageCounts: 2 user/reply before reading; 1 updated reply after explicit latest then scrolling back; 3 after a second unread user/reply
checks.keyboardLatest: Shift+Tab from composer focuses latest; Enter displays segment 180 and clears count
checks.keyboardPageEnd: Tab navigation then Enter returns older page to message 109, not newest history page
checks.pagination: Message 108 with same visible offset restored after newer -> older
checks.eviction: Four session views visited; returning long conversation preserves segment 115. Exact 3-view ownership additionally asserted by Electron E2E.
